# Cognition Therapeutics Announces Issuance of Composition of Matter Patent, Extending Protection for Zervimesine (CT1812) Through 2045


– An additional five years of patent protection may be possible through a standard extension –


October 13, 2026 06:00 ET


PURCHASE, N.Y., Oct. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) —[Cognition Therapeutics, Inc.](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=stZHOjW44mD2vX9FKgd2S9ZvYYMN6qUf_WuXFDjh8xjPIeK-Guh0FXGcOr1Uyp5Kej2RW21gMPDiD7twBwwHzdT2Fsc8WKSohkvv-LBNDXTNwJB_OqYEsnH7wQ7xEBQv) , (the “Company” or “Cognition”) (NASDAQ: CGTX), a clinical-stage company developing drugs that treat neurodegenerative disorders, announced that the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) has granted the company a patent covering a novel crystalline form, or polymorph, of zervimesine (CT1812), the company’s lead drug candidate. The patent has a natural expiration of 2045. Upon zervimesine’s approval by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), the patent may be eligible for an extension of up to five additional years.


“The form of zervimesine covered by this patent has an enhanced pharmaceutical and physiochemical profile, which is more suitable for the large-scale manufacturing required for Phase 3 and commercialization,” said[Anthony Caggiano, M.D., Ph.D.](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=VpozTlT7y2pMg6fHap18C1-cUbqHjJPJux0Wsn8C8I1ORm17bFUN10Y1SC3s4h-rw1ki18z-kd50aVwBVqPeq1t-2Tmlr6S6oj_4SddjMqAFA6WnBTJhqbvQGg0oS9UNAUTbKSduYH1i6ec0aTPSLg==) , Cognition’s chief medical officer. “We have a meeting scheduled with the FDA next week to finalize endpoint selection for our registrational program in dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB). Pending a favorable outcome from this meeting, we plan to begin manufacturing this new form of zervimesine in the first quarter of 2027 for use in our registrational clinical trial.”


The patent, titled *“Crystalline forms of 2-(tert-butoxy)-4-(3-methyl-3-(5-(methylsulfonyl)isoindolin-2-yl)butyl)phenol fumarate salt,”* has been assigned U.S. Patent No. 12,759,979.


The ‘979 patent offers the following protections:


- **Composition of Matter:** a polymorphic crystalline form of zervimesine.
- **Production Process:** a proprietary process for producing this form of zervimesine.
- **Therapeutic Methods:** methods of treating the age-related degenerative disorders Alzheimer’s disease, dry age-related macular degeneration (dry AMD), and dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB)


**About Cognition Therapeutics**
[Cognition Therapeutics, Inc.](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=stZHOjW44mD2vX9FKgd2S9ZvYYMN6qUf_WuXFDjh8xiKQ6OoNg51mIebQ-l2FIHKj-ONv93lFhQsSLbdEUxjbgj-B3lteJN3rlhbHqDlI7vL_mwToL8GaD24u7KmETsa) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company dedicated to helping millions of families seeking effective treatments for devastating neurodegenerative diseases through the development of novel, accessible therapies. The company has led pioneering research into the underlying mechanisms of degenerative nerve disorders. Our scientific approach builds on well-established biological pathways and translates across indications in which toxic oligomers drive disease progression, offering potential in dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB), Alzheimer’s disease, geographic atrophy, Parkinson’s, among others. Backed by nearly $200 million in National Institutes of Health and related foundation grants, Cognition Therapeutics continues to advance clinical research in its efforts to bring forth solutions that meet patients where they are and reduce caregiver burden. Learn more at[cogrx.com](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=fX46aTYtx4BWhnCQBbSw_deE3IMrHvKEtTrqkP73T46CLAfVfarbOwgGv6uH-Q-xBk5DSqWILnT3vqrji1kEZA==) .


**About Zervimesine (CT1812)**
The company’s lead candidate, zervimesine (CT1812), is an investigational once-daily oral therapy that has demonstrated promise in Phase 2 clinical trials in DLB and mild-to-moderate Alzheimer’s disease.[Zervimesine](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=zHfuYyWmV9RHiZxU_zOrBMgmA4w9PwqwNXXhCCMT5YqlUVnF1QpQbN5BwqilFN_a6ePC_-s64gkFfli8h1M7B1aKoErjs7zZV-nZWA2e8iU=) (CT1812) is currently being studied in the Phase 2 START Study ([NCT05531656](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=QKX8lSTrObqCLL5fSjqIbENZ6CvXOxSfHWoX1f7-FUV7fsJnnP5pnluuP-ofthI2ZuzVTEBJvWbf3nO0jsN-gzFif3JG9TKjJ5rqDZi1T80Drtfx4s97F4LOKrYktQYW) ) in patients with MCI and early Alzheimer’s disease. Phase 2 clinical studies have concluded in dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB), mild-to-moderate Alzheimer’s disease, and geographic atrophy secondary to dry AMD. Based in part on the strong efficacy signals observed in the Phase 2 SHIMMER study in DLB ([NCT05225415](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=QKX8lSTrObqCLL5fSjqIbDZfxbp30veKj6FGLmUsOcld0Bex8wVyXPVdM8GhSSUIGMZvVwL56ej8XnKhQdgAZxssT75tmNSIjpbq0WK7LnWWZsVALhsrt8P_GA0VXEPq) ), the company plans to advance zervimesine into a registrational trial for people with DLB who experience psychosis. Zervimesine has been generally well tolerated in clinical studies to date.


The USAN Council has adopted zervimesine as the United States Adopted Name (USAN) for CT1812.
